title: KV delta-residual quantization + adaptive INT-ladder experiment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: reduce GPU KV cache footprint by ~2–4× on long-context inference while bounding quality degradation. Introduce a hybrid technique we call 'delta-residual quantization' plus an adaptive INT-ladder runtime that dynamically assigns FP8/INT8/INT4 encodings per KV block based on token salience and predicted reconstruction error. This ticket scopes the experiment matrix, instrumentation, datasets, rollout safety checks, and preliminary cost/latency targets.
plan: Design encoding: store base compressed block (INT4/INT8) plus a small residual stream kept in FP16 for high-salience positions (delta-residual). The residual stream is sparsely populated and decays for older tokens.

Adaptive ladder runtime: runtime policy evaluates per-request scoring vector (token_snr_estimate, position_importance, recent_reuse_frequency) and picks encoding level per-shard: FP8 -> INT8 -> INT4. Policy tunable by percentile thresholds and budget cap.

Integration with continuous batching: ensure dynamic encoding decisions are cheap (<200ns per shard) and composable with batching path. Add a pre-batch pass that annotates requests with preferred encoding hints; fallback to default bucket when budget exhausted.

Build instrumentation: kv_q_v2 metrics that track encoded_size_bytes, residual_bytes, mean_recon_error, token_level_logp_delta, request_level_perplexity_delta, and QoS (latency tail impact). Emit per-model and per-cohort aggregates.

Experiment matrix: run across FP8/INT8/INT4 base compressions x residual thresholds (0.1%, 0.5%, 1% token retention) x policy aggressiveness (conservative/medium/aggressive). Target models: rdx-gpt-3.5-ff (16k), open-llm-70b (32k).

Evaluation: measure generation quality vs baseline (no compression) on held-out eval sets (SQuAD-style QA, long-form summarization, code completion) and on production-like prompt traces from anonymized session cohorts.

Safety: define hard guardrails for rollback: if >0.8% absolute drop in exact-match for QA or >2.0 increase in avg token logloss percentile relative to baseline, disable aggressive modes and surface to oncall.
Deliverables: experiment artifacts include evaluation notebook, perf dashboards, PR with runtime changes gated behind feature flag 'kv_delta_resid_v1'.
evaluation_criteria: Memory savings: median per-request KV memory reduction >= 2× (aggressive) or >=1.5× (conservative) relative to baseline FP16 cache
Quality: generation-level metrics within acceptable deltas: QA EM drop <= 0.7% (aggressive) / <=0.3% (conservative); average token logp increase <= 1.0 nats (aggressive) / <=0.4 nats (conservative)
Latency: added per-request encoding/decoding overhead < 1.5ms median when batching preserved; p95 latency increase <= 10%
Cost: projected token-cost reduction on Dedicated GPU pools >= 18% for common long-context workloads
Stability: no significant growth in token-level variance across requests; regression alerts triggered for outlier cohorts
datasets_and_traces: Internal: anonymized production trace sample (prod-cohorts-perf-2026-02) — sampled with privacy-preserving filters
Synthetic: stress sequences with adversarial reuse patterns to probe residual efficacy
instrumentation_and_logging: alert: kv-delta-resid-regression if model-level EM drop exceeds thresholds
experiment_buckets: b1: conservative ladder (FP8 default, INT8 targets only for low-salience)
b2: medium ladder (FP8 -> INT8 -> INT4 tiers with 0.5% residual retention)
b3: aggressive ladder (favor INT4 with 1% residual reservoir for top-salient tokens)
b4: ablation: base INT4 without residual stream to measure residual value

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: reconstruction errors concentrated on named entities or code tokens => mitigation: extend residual retention to include heuristics (capitalization, punctuation-heavy tokens) and add feature to reserve residuals for tokens with rare subtoken IDs.
Risk: increased latency tails when many requests attempt to access residual stream concurrently => mitigation: shard-reservoir with LRU eviction and budgeted reads per-request
Risk: interaction with KV eviction policies causing oscillation => mitigation: add hysteresis and decay windows to encoding policy and simulate with traffic replay harness
Risk: deployment complexity across Dedicated/Private clusters => mitigation: keep implementation behind a runtime feature flag and provide simple knobbed policies for enterprise customers
rollout_plan: Feature behind flag: kv_delta_resid_v1. Start on staging models only.
Phase 1: canary on synthesized low-risk cohorts (1% traffic) for 48h. Verify metrics and no unexpected errors.
Phase 2: extend to 10% internal traffic for 7 days with daily checks on quality and infra costs.
Phase 3: optionally widen to production cohorts once thresholds satisfied. Provide opt-out by customer for Private deployments.
Rollback: automated disable if quality or latency thresholds breached for >2 consecutive checks
